title: Configure Generator
description:
Change settings by adjusting numbers or changing "true" and "false". Do not change the card in any other way. Below are detailed explanations of each setting.

General Settings
> Description Size
 - (number, 10+)
 - The base number of words the AI will try to output for descriptive fields.
 - These fields are marked with a (D) in the Outline story card.
 - Large numbers here will require larger context sizes to work.

> Include Story Request in JSON
- (true or false)
- Includes the player's initial Story Request in the final JSON output.
- It will be placed as a field at the top of the Overview section.
- Only works if the player entered a story request on initial scenario creation.

Seed Word Settings
> Add Random Seed Words
- (true or false)
- If enabled, a list of random seed words will be added to the prompt.
- New seeds are generated every action.
- This is meant to add variety to the AI's generations
- Seed words are randomly selected from the enabled word lists.
- Seed words are not shown to the player by default.
- WARNING: retry behavior is unpredictable.
- AI dungeon caches multiple outputs at once to let you retry more quickly.
- Cached retries all share the same seed word list.

> Use SFW List
- (true or false)
- Whether the SFW word list should be included in the seed word pool.
- If all lists are set false, this list will be used.

> Use NSFW List
- (true or false)
- Whether the SFW word list should be included in the seed word pool.

> Seed Word Count
- (number, 1-50)
- How many seed words will be selected for the seed word list.

> Show Seed Words
- (true or false)
- If enabled, the seed words will be shown to the player.
- The seed words will be show on a comment line (starting with "//")
- These lines are hidden from the AI and ecluded from the final JSON

Overview
> Tags: Preserve supplied tags. If none were supplied, generate up to ten important tags, separated by commas.
> Dungeon: The proper name of the Dungeon.
> Thronebound: The proper name of the Thronebound.
> Homeworld: The proper name of the Thronebound's origin world.
> Concept: (D-10)The central concept tying together the Dungeon, Thronebound, and their origin.

Dungeon Template
> Theme: The Dungeon's primary overarching theme or concept.
> Style: The Dungeon's overarching architectural, environmental, and aesthetic style.
> Population: The collective name the Thronebound uses for the Dungeon's manifested population. Preserve any supplied name exactly. It may be a simple species or nature term such as Undead, Drones, Giant Ants, or Constructs, or a longer proper collective name such as The Daughters of the Veil. Output only the name.
> Population Appearance: (D+20)The typical shared appearance and visual characteristics used as the basis for Dungeon population, cohorts, and summoned Administrators.
> Description: (D+70)The Dungeon's overall atmosphere, physical identity, recurring materials, forms, motifs, and sensory qualities.
> Manifestation: (D)How the Dungeon's Theme and Style generally express themselves through its structures, population, objects, magic, technology, or environment.
> Throne Room: (D+30)The appearance and atmosphere of the starting Throne Room as the Dungeon's first manifested space.

Dungeon Resources
> Construction Name: The name of the Dungeon's Construction resource.
> Construction Description: (D-20)...
> Construction Collection: How it is produced, gathered, created, or obtained.
> Construction Use: How its themed nature supports the fixed DMS role of paying for facility construction, Expansion, Tier Ups, fortifications, equipment structures, and other structural work.
> Sustenance Name: The name of the Dungeon's Sustenance resource.
> Sustenance Description: (D-20)...
> Sustenance Collection: How it is produced, gathered, created, or obtained.
> Sustenance Use: How its themed nature supports the fixed DMS role of population upkeep, cohort maintenance, resilience, and recovery.
> Development Name: The name of the Dungeon's Development resource.
> Development Description: (D-20)...
> Development Collection: How it is produced, gathered, created, or obtained.
> Development Use: How its themed nature supports the fixed DMS role of Thronebound and Administrator growth, Class and ability development, Bond or Rank advancement, research, and related refinement.
> Energy Name: The name of the Dungeon's ungraded primary Energy currency.
> Energy Description: (D-20)Describe the Dungeon-themed power that serves as its primary internal currency.
> Energy Collection: How the Dungeon generates, channels, or acquires this usable power.
> Energy Use: How it serves as the primary Dungeon currency used throughout construction, facility operation and upgrades, summoning, training, research, portals, and Dungeon advancement.

Character Template
> Race: The Thronebound's race or species.
> Gender: ...
> Appearance: (D+80)...
> Personality: (D+20)...
> Background: (D+50)The important history of the Thronebound before becoming bound to the Dungeon.
> Capabilities: (D+20)Important abilities, training, magic, technology, knowledge, or other capabilities possessed before Dungeon progression.
> Values: (D)Important motivations, priorities, attachments, ambitions, and personal values.
> Voice Pattern: (D+10)Direct description without metaphor, analogy, or examples.

Unique Attributes
> Primary Name: The Dungeon's strongest defining Unique Attribute. It must express a Dungeon-theme power or influence and must not duplicate Might, Agility, Endurance, Arcana, Command, Logistics, Insight, or Craft.
> Primary Description: (D)...
> Primary Aptitude: One Aptitude from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, or SSS.
> Secondary Name: A second nonredundant Dungeon-theme Unique Attribute, or N/A.
> Secondary Description: ...
> Secondary Aptitude: One Aptitude from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, or SSS, or N/A.
> Tertiary Name: A third nonredundant Dungeon-theme Unique Attribute, or N/A.
> Tertiary Description: ...
> Tertiary Aptitude: One Aptitude from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, or SSS, or N/A.

Aptitudes
> Might: One Aptitude from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, or SSS.
> Agility: One Aptitude from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, or SSS.
> Endurance: One Aptitude from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, or SSS.
> Arcana: One Aptitude from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, or SSS.
> Command: One Aptitude from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, or SSS.
> Logistics: One Aptitude from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, or SSS.
> Insight: One Aptitude from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, or SSS.
> Craft: One Aptitude from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, or SSS.

Attribute Growth Preference
> Favored Attributes: Select up to five Attributes best suited to the Thronebound's preferred future development. May include standard Attributes and generated Unique Attributes. Names only, separated by commas.

Homeworld
> Description: (D+60)Describe the Thronebound's origin world, including its environment, societies, magic, technology, and other defining characteristics relevant to the character.
> Region: (D+20)The broader region most relevant to the Thronebound.
> Primary Anchor: (D+20)The specific location the Thronebound is anchored to on their Homeworld and normally returns to when opening a gate back to it.
> Residence: (D+10)The Thronebound's home or normal private living space at the Primary Anchor. Use 'None' if they have no stable home.
> Time Period: A specific year, named era, or period.
> Current Circumstances: (D+20)Important current conditions affecting the Thronebound or their Homeworld.
title: Outline
description:
🌍 Overview
>The generator uses the outline as a template. It follows the outline, creating each section and field listed, using the instructions provided for each field to generate their entries.

📋 Expected Structure
> The outline expects three types of text arranged like this:
    Section
    Field: Instructions
    Field: Instructions

    Section
    Field: Instructions
    Field: Instructions
> Sections categorize the fields that follow them. They are in title case, have two linebreaks between them and the last field, and they are followed by fields. They cannot use colons (":").
> Fields are the topics which contain instructions for the AI. Fields follow sections and end with a colon.
> Instructions let the AI know any specific rules about how it should produce entries for their field. They are all of the text after a field's colon and before the end of the line.

🧍 Character Template
> The Character Template is a special section of the outline.
> It is used to create Protagonist and supporting character sections within the scenario.
> Supporting characters are determined by the Supporting Characters field of the Overview
> DO NOT change the Character Template section name.

⚗️ Changing the Outline
> Feel free to change around the outline to get the generator to make a prompt that is more to your liking. 
> Fields, sections, and instructions can be added, removed, or changed, so long as they follow the expected structure.
> WARNING: Changing fields and sections above the generator's current position in the outline won't cause it to go back and generate the missing fields.
> For best effect, only change or add text below the generator's current position.

🎊 Special Instructions
> Special notation may optionally be used for Instructions.
> Instructions of "..." means the AI won't be given any special instructions for filling out a field. The AI is pretty clever, and it usually does a pretty good job without special instructions.
> "(D)" at the start of instructions tells the AI to write a description and gives it a word count target. By default, the base word count target is 50. The base value can be changed in the config card, but each field's description size can also be modified individually. To do this, put +/- and a number after the D.
> For example, with default settings, instructions of "(D-20)..." tells the AI to write a 30-word description, and gives it no further instructions on what that description should contain.
